headline: Tolan secures $30M in funding to scale its AI companion app
summary: The AI companion app, which helps users navigate life and relationships, has now raised $30 million, pushing its valuation past $268 million.
details: Tolan, an AI companion designed to assist users with daily life, relationships, and goals, has successfully raised $30 million in new funding. This latest round, which includes investments from Union Square Ventures, Khosla Ventures, and Homebrew, doubles the startup's total capital raised and significantly increases its valuation.

While the company has not officially disclosed its new valuation, reports estimate it to be over $268 million. Tolan generates revenue through tiered memberships, offering full access to its features. The company reported its annual recurring revenue is now in the "double-digit millions."

Tolan boasts over 250,000 active users who have engaged in more than 70 million conversations in the past year. Approximately 70% of its user base are women, with 40% being parents. The app is noted for its ability to provide support and organizational assistance, particularly appealing to neurodivergent individuals.

The app's cartoonish character aims to offer support without being perceived as overly strange, differentiating it from competitors like Friend, which faced public criticism. Tolan seeks to strike a balance between being a helpful tool and maintaining user comfort.

The AI companion space is becoming increasingly competitive, with companies like Meta developing their own AI agents with avatars. Tolan must continue to innovate to stand out amidst emerging AI agents that offer task planning and organization alongside conversational support.

Tolan also faces the significant challenge of navigating the risks associated with providing AI-powered emotional support. Lawsuits have been filed against similar AI app makers, alleging that chatbot interactions have contributed to user harm.

headline_marked: [[Mercury 3]] LLM beats GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 at 1000+ tokens/sec
headline: Mercury 3 LLM beats GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 at 1000+ tokens/sec
summary: The new diffusion-based LLM boasts 4-8x faster speeds and a 50% launch discount on its token pricing.
details: Inception has launched Mercury 3, a diffusion-based LLM that claims to outperform GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5. It achieves speeds of over 1,000 tokens per second, reportedly running 4-8x faster than its competitors.

Mercury 3 is over 40x larger than its predecessor, Mercury 1, demonstrating that text diffusion models can scale effectively for complex use cases. The company states that the scaling laws that drove progress in autoregressive models also apply to diffusion models.

Early access partners are already utilizing Mercury 3 for various applications, including voice and chat support, real-time tutoring, data engineering, and web navigation. Its speed is crucial for latency-sensitive applications like browser agents and interactive education platforms.
In web navigation tasks, Mercury 3 reportedly completed 50% of live Mind2Web navigation tasks, significantly more than GPT-6.1-Sol, using the same token volume and agent steps but at a lower cost.

For educational purposes, Mercury 3 provides instant feedback, with responses in about a second, enabling faster learning loops for students. This speed is critical for keeping students engaged without long waiting times.

Search applications benefit from Mercury 3's speed, allowing for the processing of dozens of documents within user engagement timeframes. In smart glasses tests, it achieved a median generation time of 0.9 seconds and an end-to-end response time of 2.2 seconds.

Customer support applications, particularly in regulated industries, require fast and accurate responses. Mercury 3 has been shown to provide conversational responses without sacrificing accuracy, outperforming other models in latency and performance evaluations.

Mercury 3 is the flagship model for Inception's real-time AI product portfolio. This includes Mercury Voice, optimized for extreme low-latency voice applications, and Mercury Decide, a high-volume classification decision model.

Mercury 3 is available starting today. The launch price is $0.10 per 1 million input tokens and $0.35 per 1 million output tokens, a 50% discount from the standard pricing of $0.20 per 1 million input and $0.70 per 1 million output tokens.
